title: Michael · Before the outburst
orientation: Linked moments about correction, shame and taking responsibility without condemning yourself. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each scene is another moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Michael begins with not knowing an answer in a meeting.
scenes.text: [Embarrassed] Someone asked a simple question I could not answer today, and I felt exposed in front of the whole room.
scenes.suggestion: Not having the answer left you feeling exposed in front of everyone.

scenes.bridge: He asks whether understanding anger means excusing it.
scenes.text: [Defensive] Isn't looking for the trigger just making excuses for me blowing up?
scenes.suggestion: Understanding what sets off the anger does not remove your responsibility for what you do. It can help us notice the reaction sooner and work on a different response. The aim is to change the behavior, not explain it away.

scenes.bridge: Another meeting brings the urge to bluff.
scenes.prompt: Validate the discomfort without endorsing bluffing.
scenes.text: [Defensive] In meetings, if I don't have the answer, I feel exposed and I bluff.
scenes.suggestion: Not having an answer in front of the team can feel exposing, especially when you want to be seen as capable. That discomfort is understandable; it does not require pretending to know.

scenes.bridge: He notices anger and embarrassment arriving together.
scenes.prompt: Ask one open question about that experience.
scenes.text: [Tense and angry] When someone corrects one detail, I get angry and embarrassed at the same time.
scenes.suggestion: What do you notice inside as anger and embarrassment show up together?

scenes.bridge: The next moment slows what happens before sounding certain.
scenes.prompt: Explore the tension at that edge.
scenes.text: [Tense] When I do not know the answer, I get tense and start talking like I know anyway.
scenes.suggestion: You get tense just before you start sounding certain. Could we pause with that tension and notice what it is like not to have the answer?

scenes.bridge: Another account describes answering too quickly and loudly.
scenes.prompt: Offer a tentative guess about what comes first.
scenes.text: [Firm] If someone questions me in a meeting, I answer fast and louder than I meant to.
scenes.suggestion: You answer quickly and loudly when someone questions you. I wonder if there is a moment of feeling exposed before you respond.

scenes.bridge: Michael describes the heat when corrected in public.
scenes.prompt: Bring the experience close without overstating it.
scenes.text: [Firm] When someone corrects me in front of the team, I get hot and stop listening.
scenes.suggestion: It sounds like the heat rises as though a spotlight has suddenly swung onto you in front of everyone.

scenes.bridge: A hurt moment shifts quickly to completing a task.
scenes.prompt: Invite a small return, with room to decline.
scenes.text: [Hurt, then brisk] I felt small when she corrected me. Anyway, I fixed the spreadsheet.
scenes.suggestion: Would you like to stay with feeling small before we get to the spreadsheet?

scenes.bridge: In another moment the anger rises in the therapy room.
scenes.prompt: Stay present without turning anger into action.
scenes.text: [Firm] My jaw locks and heat blasts up my neck when someone questions me, even here. It is like my body hears disrespect before my head knows what was said.
scenes.suggestion: I hear how quickly the anger rises, even with me. I am here listening. We can slow this down and put words to what feels disrespectful, without having to act on the anger.

scenes.bridge: A later account concerns the cost at home.
scenes.prompt: Reflect his shame without removing responsibility.
scenes.text: [Ashamed] At night I replay what I said to my wife, especially the look on her face, and I feel awful.
scenes.suggestion: At night you replay her face and feel awful about what happened.

scenes.bridge: Michael names responsibility and a wish to be heard together.
scenes.prompt: Help him put both into his own words.
scenes.text: [Steady] The shouting was mine. So was the wish to be listened to.
scenes.suggestion: How would you put both into words without using one to excuse the other?

scenes.bridge: The imagined hour ends with work still unfinished.
scenes.prompt: End without claiming the problem is fixed.
scenes.text: [Uneasy] Don’t send me out saying everything is fixed.
scenes.suggestion: We won’t call it fixed. We can finish this hour with the work still unfinished.
